messages:
Dana (People Ops): Heads up — Jorge Ramos received his PTO cashout on 2026-02-28 and net pay was much lower than expected. Looks like the cashout was taxed as supplemental (flat federal 22%) instead of aggregated with regular wages. Can payroll confirm? @Miguel
Miguel (Payroll): Give me emp id + last4 SSN and the run id? I can pull the ledger.
Dana (People Ops): emp id 50177, last4 4412, run PR-2026-02-28-02. PTO cashout gross 4,200. Jorge reported federal withheld $924 which matches 22% flat, but his normal effective withholding would be closer to ~12% (~$504). That's ~ $420 overwithheld. State CA also looks higher.
Payroll Bot: Ledger extract PR-2026-02-28-02:
```Earnings:
  PTO_CASHOUT 4200
Taxes:
  Fed_Withholding 924
  CA_Withholding 210
Notes: PTO cashout flagged as SUPPLEMENTAL for that run (pay code mapping SUPPL->SUPP_TAX)```
Miguel (Payroll): Confirmed. Our pay engine treated PTO_CASHOUT as supplemental because the paycode mapping defaulted during the February pay config change. Sorry about that. Options: 1) Issue a manual refund for the overwithheld tax amounts in March off-cycle (gross-up not needed because we're returning withheld taxes only). 2) Process a corrective payroll adjustment and then issue a W-2c to adjust box 1/2 and state boxes. We should also correct employer tax remittance records.
Zoe (Finance): For books we prefer a corrective payroll entry so the ledgers tie out (debit payroll liability to cash). If we do a refund, please include supporting journal PR-ADJ-2026-03-08. Also check payroll tax deposits: if the deposit was already submitted, we must file an adjustment with the tax agencies or wait for quarterly reconciliation depending on timing.
Miguel (Payroll): Plan: I'll create PR-ADJ-2026-03-08 to reverse the supplemental flag and re-run a net-pay refund for Jorge of $420 federal + $60 state (est) net = $480.
I'll attach the journal and create case PR-CASE-6901. If W-2 box 1 remains correct (we're only fixing withholding), we may not need a W-2c; but if the grossing method affected taxable wages, we'll do W-2c. Estimated timeline: refund run in 3 business days after approval; tax remittance impact TBD.
Dana (People Ops): Please cc Jorge on the communications and include a plain-language explanation + suggested steps in case he already filed taxes. He asked whether he needs to amend — what do we recommend?
Zoe (Finance): Recommend: if Jorge hasn't filed, no action likely needed once we refund and provide corrected W-2 (if W-2c needed). If he already filed, advise him to consult tax advisor; provide an estimate letter of withheld amounts and our case number. We'll include that in the email.
Miguel (Payroll): Created PR-ADJ-2026-03-08 and PR-CASE-6901. Looping Legal for the employee note. Processing refund run on 2026-03-10 if approvals come through.
Dana (People Ops): Thanks — please paste the final message here before sending to Jorge so I can review.
